headline: Anthropic's unpublished IPO prospectus warns that how the US government views the company could hurt its ties with customers and partners, Reuters reports.
score_reason: Kept at 8: a Reuters exclusive from the prospectus of one of the biggest AI companies, supported by consistent detail in follow-up coverage; the prospectus itself is not public.
importance_line: It tells investors, Anthropic's business customers and government agencies that Anthropic itself sees political friction as a business risk, but the prospectus is not public and Reuters says government work is under 1% of its revenue.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by The Next Web, that Anthropic's IPO prospectus, which is not public, warns that how the US government views the company could spill over and harm its ties with business customers, partners and others, even though government deals are under 1% of its yearly revenue. This adds to the 29 Sep 2026 reporting on the same prospectus; The Next Web's account says the filing cites the Pentagon's supply-chain-risk label, which a judge temporarily blocked in March, and June export controls that led Anthropic to switch off two top models for all customers until 1 July.
notes: Original outlet Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/anthropic-warns-government-attitudes-may-hurt-customer-ties-ipo-prospectus-shows-2026-10-02/) returned HTTP 401; wrote from The Next Web's account of the Reuters exclusive (and a short Yahoo Finance item), so source and url are The Next Web's. The Next Web says it has not seen the prospectus. Continues the 29 Sep 2026 Reuters story on the same prospectus; the new part is the government-relations risk.
